descriptionChirho: Abstract noun denoting the action or process of boasting, glorying, or exulting. Greek καύχησις (distinct from καύχημα which is the object of boasting) emphasizes the activity itself. Spanish 'jactancia' (boasting, bragging); Hindi घमण्ड / घमण्ड की शपथ (pride, boasting, oath of pride); Arabic الافتِخارِ / فَخرِكُم (the boasting, your boasting); Korean 자랑이 / 자랑을 / 자랑의 (boasting as subject/object/possessive); Swahili kujisifu (the act of self-praise). S70592 covers the standard case forms (nominative, accusative, genitive) and S70594 is a single accusative occurrence; both are purely grammatical inflections of the same abstract concept. Found throughout Paul's letters (Rom 3:27; 1 Cor 15:31; 2 Cor 1:12, 7:4, 7:14, 8:24, 11:10, 11:17; 1 Thess 2:19; Jas 4:16).
